item.title: The OpenSat4Weather dataset: Ku-band satellite link data for precipitation monitoring
item.description:
The OpenSat4Weather dataset: Ku-band satellite link data for precipitation monitoring
Roberto Nebuloni, Maximilian Graf, Greta Cazzaniga, François Mercier, and Maxime Turko
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7455–7473, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7455-2026, 2026
We describe the OpenSat4Weather public dataset, which provides time series of received power from 215 TV-SAT satellite microwave links located in Southern France over a five-month observation period and at 1-min resolution. These data can be processed to gather indirect rainfall intensity measurements. OpenSat4Weather also includes concurrent data from operational rain gauges and weather radars, and ERA5 0°C isotherm height data, to derive the wet fraction of the satellite-to-ground path.

item.title: Atlas of geochemical, petrophysical and mechanical rock properties of the crystalline basement in Germany – first release
item.description:
Atlas of geochemical, petrophysical and mechanical rock properties of the crystalline basement in Germany – first release
Leandra Maren Weydt, Ángel Andrés Ramírez-Guzmán, Lena Muhl, Fiorenza Deon, Anja Maria Schleicher, and Ingo Sass
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-555,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
The AMPEDEK database is the first standardized, open-access database of rock properties for Germany's crystalline basement. By combining published data with new laboratory measurements, it provides 25,700 petrophysical and mechanical data points, as well as geochemical and mineralogical data, from more than 8,200 samples collected across eight federal states. The database supports preliminary reservoir assessments and future exploration campaigns for a wide range of geological applications.

item.title: marinedb: An open-source, flexible and scalable Python workflow for curating, standardizing, and integrating marine biodiversity data
item.description:
marinedb: An open-source, flexible and scalable Python workflow for curating, standardizing, and integrating marine biodiversity data
Elena Berhocoïrigoin, Philippe Le Noac'h, Martin Laviale, Sakina-Dorothée Ayata, Jérémy Fix, and Cédric Pradalier
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-771,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Knowing where marine species live helps us understand and protect ocean life, but the underlying records are spread across sources, vary widely in how they were collected, described, and formatted, and are affected by data-quality issues. We developed marinedb, an open tool for cleaning biodiversity data, and used it to build a global dataset of nearly 159 million records covering more than 139,000 species, making large-scale studies of marine species distributions easier and more reproducible.

item.title: A High-Resolution Gridded Dataset of Vertically Resolved Fine Root Biomass Across China
item.description:
A High-Resolution Gridded Dataset of Vertically Resolved Fine Root Biomass Across China
Wenlu Zheng, Min Zhao, Woheng Li, Deshuai Zhang, Weihua Tang, Junshen Luo, Shuning Jiao, Fengtai Li, and Haicheng Zhang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-777,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Fine roots help plants take up water and nutrients and store carbon in soil. We developed a dataset showing the vertical distribution of fine roots across China from 2005–2025. Using thousands of field measurements and environmental data, we mapped root biomass in 20 cm layers down to 2 m. The dataset reveals strong differences in root distribution among regions and plant types and provides a new resource for understanding belowground carbon storage and ecosystem change.

item.title: TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023: Improved species range mapping in a tree-level forest dataset for the conterminous United States
item.description:
TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023: Improved species range mapping in a tree-level forest dataset for the conterminous United States
Karin Riley, Rachel Houtman, Scott Zimmer, Lila Leatherman, Jamie Peeler, John Shaw, Isaac Grenfell, Maria Borja Arboleda, Abhinav Shrestha, Ian Housman, and Mark Finney
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-633,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 1 comment)
New TreeMap datasets provide imputed 30 m gridded maps with modeled tree-level detail for forests across the conterminous United States in 2020, 2022, and 2023. Updated methods improve climate data inputs, independent validation approaches, and species range mapping. These improvements strengthen TreeMap’s use in Earth system applications such as carbon cycling, wildfire behavior, and habitat distribution modeling, which depend on accurate representations of forest composition and structure.
